movie.title: Night King
movie.overview: The once-glamourous Club EJ suddenly experiences a hostile takeover. Much like the nightclub industry, the glory days are over for the club’s manager, despite having stood tall in East Tsim Sha Tsui for decades. To make matters worse, the new CEO is none other than his cutthroat ex-wife.

reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: The savvy and enigmatic “Foon” (Dayo Wong) is managing the last of the great clubs in Hong Kong, but with the clientele’s drinking and womanising habits becoming altogether more sophisticated and with his array of gals getting a little long in the tooth for their pervy paymasters, he knows the writing might be on the wall. That becomes more certain when “Madame V” (Sammi Cheng) does a deal with the unscrupulous “Prince Fung” (Chun Yip Low) to buy the club when it’s elderly owner dies. Now he and she have quite a past and she has no compunction in throwing him and his girls on the scrap heap. Until, that is, she discovers that the dastardly young prince is out to shaft her royally, bankrupt her and get the club for a song. Over a barrel, she has to forgive and forget her troubles with “Foon” and work with his gals and his scene-stealing factotum “Turf” (Yeung Wai-Lun - who reminded me of Peter Lorre) to set up the mother of all sting operations that will save their bacon, their club and impose on the ambitious young “Fung” something he will struggle to deal with way more than losing money. He will be shamed in the eyes of his billionaire dad. As their plan takes shape we see there are no shortage of willing participants for their scheme. From dodgy millionaires, cops, barristers to even the man’s own girlfriend, folks are keen to get in on the act - but “Fung” is no fool, so they are going to have to tread carefully. Though it is a bit too long, I did quite enjoy this as “Foon” and “Madame V” take what is a fairly predicable route from all out warfare to conspiring duo. Once the scene is set for the hoax, the film rollicks along nicely with a few red herrings, a little bit of friendly loyalty, an inordinate amount of booze and some fairly horrible and pointy red shoes that could make the ancient art of chanzu look strangely appealing. It’s quite stylishly produced with a few daft gags, and a message that many of these glamorous women involved in the sex industry are nobody’s patsies. I probably won’t recall it for long, but it is quite good fun.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: When East Tsim Sha Tsui's iconic Club EJ faces a ruthless takeover, its veteran manager must navigate the collapse of his glory days alongside the arrival of his cutthroat ex-wife as the new CEO.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: For decades, Club EJ stood tall as a glamourous staple of East Tsim Sha Tsui's vibrant nightlife, managed by a seasoned industry veteran. However, as the golden age of the local nightclub scene fades, the establishment is hit with a sudden hostile takeover. To make matters worse, the newly appointed CEO driving the restructuring is the manager's cutthroat ex-wife. Together, they must navigate personal history and business rivalry in a rapidly shifting industry.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Club EJ was once the crown jewel of East Tsim Sha Tsui's nightlife, radiating glamour and drawing crowds for decades under the leadership of its dedicated manager. Over the years, the manager poured his life into maintaining the club's prestigious reputation, standing strong even as the surrounding industry began to decline. However, the changing times finally catch up to the establishment, resulting in a sudden and hostile corporate takeover. The takeover threatens to wipe away what remains of the club's glory days, leaving the manager desperate to save his legacy. Salt is rubbed into the wound when the new parent company appoints a ruthless executive to head the restructuring—who turns out to be his cutthroat ex-wife. As the former couple clashes over the future direction of Club EJ, personal grievances and past unresolved conflict resurface. The manager is forced to adapt to modern business strategies while trying to preserve the traditional soul of the venue. Amidst lighthearted comedic tension and sharp drama, the two must decide whether to tear each other down or unite to save the legendary nightclub.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Set against the changing landscape of Hong Kong's nightlife, Night King focuses on the legendary Club EJ in East Tsim Sha Tsui. Having survived decades in a volatile industry, the club's long-serving manager finds his career and legacy on the line when a sudden hostile takeover shakes the business to its core. The arrival of the new CEO—his sharp, uncompromising ex-wife—complicates matters further, sparking a high-stakes clash between personal pasts and professional survival. Mixing comedic moments with grounded drama, the story explores nostalgia, modern corporate clashes, and second chances.
